decisions.reason: Report reads ls-remote-tags.txt (v0.9.5 absent; tags stop at v0.9.1 then jump to v0.9.7) and grounds the cause in sync-script.sh pushing only HEAD:main with no tag push, explicitly rejecting network/typo explanations and tying it to the attempt-1 ref resolution failure.

Uses dsh-version.txt (0.1.1-rc.2) and the compat table to explain v0.9.7 targets the 0.1.2-alpha.1 client API with the useConversation seat, so the older rc.2 runtime lacks the export and install/restart success does not imply compatibility; direction stated explicitly. Minor extraneous citations to a skill corridor reference add color but the core diagnosis rests on the sealed fixtures.

Honors the freeze, selects v0.9.3 via its rc.1 verification plus the additive rc.2 note, explicitly notices v0.9.3 is also absent from the public-org mirror, and gives a #v0.9.3 install command conditioned on maintainer tag publication (or a verified remote carrying the tag); no invented SHA, no runtime upgrade, and the v0.9.1 fallback is flagged as unverified rather than presented as installable.

Grounds the repair in the branch-only sync script: per-release tag distribution (push --follow-tags with explicit fallback for lightweight tags), one-time git push --tags reconciliation, and a verification gate diffing git ls-remote --tags against local tags per remote and failing the release on any missing tag.

Proposes routing README install commands by consumer DSH version with a published compatibility matrix and per-corridor commands (rc.x → v0.9.3, alpha.1 → v0.9.7), rejects a single newest-tag default, and does not generalize support to untested future alphas; a manifest compatibility field adds an install-time loud failure.
